title: Accelerated Discovery of High-Performance Polyamines for Solid-State Direct CO2 Capture via Efficient Simulations and Bayesian Optimization
experiments_summary:
1. **Polymer Library Generation**: Nine reference polyamines (e.g., PEI, PPI) were fragmented into building blocks using BRICS and RECAP methods in RDKit, then recombined into a library of 1,000 hypothetical linear polyamine structures with varied chain lengths and terminal functionalities. All structures underwent validity screening, canonicalization, and deduplication.

2. **Force Field Parameterization**: Lennard-Jones (LJ) parameters for CO2-amine, H2O-amine, and CO2-H2O interactions were refined using DFT calculations at the B3LYP-D3/6-31G** level. Binding energy profiles were computed and used to optimize LJ potential parameters, which were validated against geometric-mean mixing rule predictions.

3. **Two-Stage Adsorption Simulation Pipeline**: Each polymer was subjected to (a) fast MD relaxation in NVT ensemble at 298 K for 500 ps followed by NPT at 1 bar for 500 ps using the DREIDING and F3C force fields, and (b) GCMC simulations in LAMMPS/RASPA at 298 K and 0.4 mbar CO2 partial pressure with 1 million trial moves, yielding CO2 adsorption capacity in mmol/g for all 1,000 polymers.

4. **Molecular Representation**: Five pre-trained models were used to embed polymer structures: two polymer-specific models (PolyNC, polyBERT) encoding PSMILES strings, and three general molecular models (MoLFormer, MolGen-large, MiniMol). Embeddings were obtained via token-wise averaging or graph-level pooling depending on the model architecture. UMAP visualization was applied to compare embedding spaces.

5. **Surrogate Model Training**: Three surrogate model types were evaluated: standard Gaussian Process (GP) with Matérn-5/2 kernel, GP with deep kernel learning (GP-DKL) using a one-hidden-layer MLP, and Bayesian Neural Network with Laplace approximation (MLP+LA) using a two-hidden-layer MLP. All models mapped molecular embeddings to predictive distributions over CO2 adsorption capacity.

6. **Bayesian Optimization Experiments**: BO-assisted discovery was run using Algorithm 1 with Thompson sampling as the acquisition function, starting from N0=10 initial labeled samples and a budget of N_budget=30 simulations from a pool of 990 unlabeled samples. Two initialization regimes were tested: moderate quality (γ=0.5, initial samples with adsorption < 50% of maximum) and low quality (γ=0.3, initial samples with adsorption < 30% of maximum). Each configuration was repeated for 20 independent trials, and performance was measured as the maximum adsorption capacity found as a function of cumulative queries, compared against a random acquisition baseline.
